text:
sophie: Customer reporting Google OAuth flow failing at token exchange with `invalid_grant`. They do the redirect to /oauth/callback?code=...&state=... then our backend POSTs to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and Google returns 400. Logs show: `PKCE validation failed: code_challenge mismatch`. They say this happens only from an embedded mobile webview (iOS WKWebView).
ryan: Do we have the original `code_challenge` we stored when issuing the auth request? can you paste the exact request/response (redact tokens) and the `code_verifier` the client generated?
sophie: Pasted snippets below (redacted):
```
GET /authorize?response_type=code&client_id=redwood&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.customer.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM&code_challenge_method=S256&state=xyz123
```
Client sends \`code_verifier\`: `dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk`
Server log when verifying (redacted):
```
[INFO] stored_code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
[INFO] computed_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw%2DcM
[ERROR] PKCE validation failed: computed != stored
```
ryan: Ah — I see `%2D` vs `-` in the computed value (URL-encoding artifact). That means somewhere we're percent-encoding the base64url output or the verifier before hashing. The computed challenge should be base64url with `-` and `_`, no percent encoding and no `=` padding.
alex: This is a pretty classic mobile/webview issue — some libraries call `encodeURIComponent()` before sending and others double-encode the challenge or verifier. Also proxy/redirect layers or the app's deep link handler can re-encode query params.
sophie: Customer says their mobile SDK uses `encodeURIcomponent` on the full redirect URL which may re-encode the `-` into `%2D` in some steps.
ryan: Steps to repro and debug for customer: 1) In the app, capture the raw `code_verifier` on the device before navigate. 2) On a reproducible run, compute the challenge locally using this command and compare to the `code_challenge` in the initial /authorize URL we recorded: 
```bash
# compute base64url(SHA256(code_verifier))
printf '%s' "<code_verifier>" | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | openssl base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='
```
If result matches the stored `code_challenge`, the client is correct. If not, the client is mangling the verifier.
alex: Also check that any deep link handler or intermediate redirect is not re-encoding the query string. A quick debug: log the exact bytes of the redirect URI received by the app and the outgoing authorize URL from the client.
sophie: For a quick server-side workaround (while they patch mobile SDK): treat `%2D` and `-` equivalently when verifying; decode percent-encodings before comparing the base64url string. But beware: decoding should happen only on the challenge string, not on the verifier prior to hashing.
ryan: Also confirm `code_challenge_method=S256` on both sides. If the client accidentally used `plain` or sent an already-hashed verifier, we'd fail.
oauth-bot: Automated note: We previously had 3 incidents in last 6 months with webview PKCE mangling. Refer to runbook PKCE-WEBVIEW-01 for triage steps.
alex: Long-term: add a small debug flag to temporarily log first 12 chars of stored challenge and computed challenge in hex to help customers without logging full secrets. We should also add automated detection: if stored contains `-` but computed contains `%`, emit a specific hint in logs to speed diagnosis.
sophie: I'm going to send the customer a few repro steps and the openssl one-liner. Will offer a small SDK patch (strip-encode) and recommend they stop calling `encodeURIComponent` on the `code_challenge`/`code_verifier` values.
ryan: Sounds good. If they can't patch quickly, we can release a short-lived tolerance change behind a feature flag for their tenant to decode percent-encodings on stored challenge verification.
sophie: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll update once customer tests the one-liner.
